title: The Only Bird Known to Sleep Through Winter
subject: common poorwill

scenes.text: One bird goes into a deep winter sleep, like a bear.
The common poorwill is a small desert nightjar. In cold snaps its body temperature can fall to about 41 degrees Fahrenheit.
Its oxygen use drops by more than 90 percent, and its heart and breathing become almost impossible to detect.
It can stay like that for weeks, living on stored fat. The Hopi called it the sleeping one.
Hummingbirds only manage short nightly naps like this. The poorwill is the only bird known to hibernate for weeks.
So when winter hits, the sleeping one just switches off.
